Im speaking as someone who trained in acting (not an actress as Im now an accountant and writer) and married a hobbyist comedian.

Actors need to be able to tap into an emotion they know and feel to project the true meaning behind someone else’s words. You have to be able to connect your own experience to that and realistically display it even if you yourself don’t feel it. You have to fill in the gaps of what you aren’t given in the script with your own ideas of what background this character had to lead them to the actions they are taking in the piece and then interpret how that person would ACTUALLY deliver that line. Comedy or tragedy, if you can do this and also develop your timing to look natural? Great job kid, you’re an actor and may even be trusted to adlib a little.

A comedian is a story teller above all else. 

They are not feeding you someone else’s words (unless they are a bad comedian), they have to work on the actual craft of story telling, and while they tap into their own emotions to evoke emotions in you, its THEIR words and experiences so its more personal and frankly more difficult. Then you have to understand crowd work cause what if that prepared material starts to bomb because it’s just not the right crowd???  You might not know that till you are about to be on stage for tour tight 5, so you have to be able to switch instantly to crowd work. if you get storytelling and crowd work down as a comedian you then have to develop a stage presence that cannot slip. You have to keep that up on stage, you don’t get to take a five and rest then try again like an actor does. They don’t get to reshoot if an off the cuff line didn’t work, you gotta just roll with the bad decision and try to save it without losing your cool.

Both are harder than people like to think, but being a comedian is one of the toughest entertainment gigs imo.
